item.title: RBI Guv opens financial inclusion camp in Maharashtra, focuses on re-KYC
item.description: Malhotra also visited stalls set up by banks, Centres for Financial Literacy (CFLs) and self-help groups (SHGs), and interacted with their representatives ...
item.dc:creator: Anjali Kumari
item.content:encoded: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday inaugurated a special financial inclusion camp at Vaksai in Maharashtra's Maval taluka, with a focus on re-KYC of bank accounts and expanding access to banking services. The camp, organised by Bank of Maharashtra on November 21 as part of the nationwide financial inclusion campaign, facilitated re-KYC of bank accounts, access to banking services and enrolment under social security schemes. Malhotra also visited stalls set up by banks, Centres for Financial Literacy (CFLs) and self-help groups (SHGs), and interacted with their representatives. The camp was attended by the managing directors and chief executive officers of Bank of Maharashtra and Bank of India, a deputy managing director of State Bank of India, and senior officials of other banks.

item.title: COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency
item.description: Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency

COP31: G77 accuses developed nations of dividing bloc, lack of transparency Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap

A COP31 sign is displayed at the venue of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 21 2026 | 11:35 PM IST

Listen to This Article

With the UN Climate Change conference (COP31) running beyond its scheduled close, developing nations have raised concerns over transparency from the presidencies to address their demands in the final outcome document. Speaking to PTI, a G77 representative alleged that developed nations are "dividing the developing nations" and hindering the process for a finance roadmap. Group of 77 (G77) is a coalition of 134 developing countries plus China at the UN that promotes members' collective economic interests and strengthens their joint negotiating power. "G77 is being divided by the European Union and High-Ambition coalition (HAC), which is an informal group of developed and developing countries within the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Meanwhile, the presidencies have also not been transparent with us," the representative said, on the condition of anonymity. Also Read

COP31 climate talks extend into overtime amid deadlock on fossil fuels

COP31: India, developing nations challenge EU on climate finance

Our development goals must move alongside sustainable future: Yadav

Nepal seeks billions at COP31; $20 mn pledged for disaster survivors so far

Global electrification push stalls at COP31 amid opposition from nations

They alleged that when the G77 called a meeting with the presidency seeking transparency on finance on Saturday, no clear answer was given to them, but they were called for consultation in groups and sub-groups selectively later. "G77 called a meeting with the COP31 presidency asking for transparency on finance, but no clear answer was given. We are concerned that what the developing nations haven't agreed to will be parachuted in the final text," the G77 official said. Expressing concerns over multiple developing nations' ministers travelling back to their home countries due to the summit running overtime, the official said, "there is a question on whether the final decision will be taken on consensus."   They further alleged that there is a lack of political will from developed nations to help developing nations combat climate change, and that the delay was a "pre-planned tactic."   The COP31 Presidency is held by Turkiye, with Murat Kurum serving as COP31 President, whereas Australia's Chris Bowen is serving as the summit's President of Negotiations.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

FBI probes suspected hack of US criminal information database: Report The FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks

FBI probes suspected hack of US criminal information database (Photo: Bloomberg)

Reuters 1 min read Last Updated : Nov 21 2026 | 10:18 PM IST

The FBI ??is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide database used by federal, state ??and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information, CNN reported on Friday, citing two people briefed on the investigation.   The apparent compromise of the National Crime Information Center database would mark the second intrusion involving an FBI system in recent months and the latest in a string of cyber incidents that have alarmed US officials over the past week.   The agency did not respond to a request for comment from Reuters.   The FBI database is used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to store and share information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.

Previous high-profile cyber disruptions over the ??past week have included a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights.   A September breach by a digital extortion group known as "ShinyHunters" accessed an FBI jobs website, compromising data on current and former FBI employees.

item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Google announces $5 mn funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research

Google announces $5 mn funding for IIT Kharagpur for advanced AI research Announced at the institute's 75th anniversary celebrations, the funding will support advanced AI research, educational opportunities and capacity building for students and researchers

As part of educational opportunities, it will support expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students and faculty (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 21 2026 | 2:01 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Technology giant Google on Saturday said it will provide IIT Kharagpur with $5 million, about ₹46 crore, to develop and accelerate advanced AI research. Speaking on the 75th anniversary of IIT Kharagpur, Director Suman Chakraborty said that the fund support for applied AI research has been envisaged by the institute's alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai. "Google is providing the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with $5 million in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research, while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent," the company said in a blog. The funding will support the institute's researchers and students across three core pillars, comprising advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building.

Under advanced AI research, the fund will support tackling critical, real-world challenges by deploying AI for Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology. Also Read

India has shown it can break limits, unlock possibilities: PM Modi

Anthropic researcher claims AI helped solve 150-year-old Riemann hypothesis

Apple plans AI agent that can browse web, control apps and write code

Anthropic shares tumble after record IPO as AI trade faces reality check

Unsiloed AI secures $7.5 million in seed funding to scale document models

As part of educational opportunities, it will support expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students and faculty. The fund will support the institute's AI frameworks and tooling to elevate the technological ecosystem across the campus. "IIT Kharagpur is driving groundbreaking work in areas like Indic languages, agriculture, and education, and Google is excited to help accelerate this impact with a new partnership. Looking forward to seeing this collaboration shape the path for the next generation of students, just as IIT Kharagpur shaped my own," Pichai said.

He said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation; programmes like this will help implement Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision that the benefits of AI reach everyone in India.
